card.name: Linking words after a stated dose or fact
card.fires_on: Short linking words or punctuation right after a complete statement, where a reason, condition or qualifier comes next. Seen mostly after dose-increase instructions (as, for, until, depending) and after a sentence of background history.

modes.label: Dose-increase qualifiers
modes.description: A linking word after an increment or dose amount that introduces a condition such as 'as needed' or 'until controlled'.
modes.example: Increase the dosage in increments of up to 75 mg per day,<< as>> needed, using another venlafax

modes.label: After a background statement
modes.description: A period or verb right after a general claim or history, where an explanation or justification follows.

modes.label: Clinical-judgment phrases
modes.description: A word inside phrases like 'if clinically indicated' that leave the choice to judgment.
modes.example: Extend the duration of the infusion if clinically<< indicated>>.

card.writes: It pushes toward words that explain reasons or benefits, such as 'benefits', 'reason for' and 'rationale'.
card.plain: It marks the point right after a statement where the text goes on to give a condition or a reason.
